headline: PONG gets the cabinet's switches
lede: The 1972 coin door had an AUTO/HUMAN selector and an Easy/Difficult RANGE switch. The arcade table now carries both: pick EASY, NORMAL, HARD or 2P from the attract screen — and NORMAL is the table everyone already knows, bit for bit.

notes.text: SHIPPED: PONG difficulty tiers + human 2-player (#3502, PR #3504). LEFT/RIGHT on attract cycles the pick; any other key or tap starts with it standing; ?diff=N pins for QA. EASY adds the cabinet's speed ceiling (5.5) and a sloppier tracker; HARD sharpens the machine; 2P seats a friend on W/S.

The default table is provably untouched: a 3000-tick trace at seed 90210 matches the pre-change replay exactly, so the seedpin law and the 39/40 driver floor stand. Measured floors pinned per tier — driver sweeps EASY 40/40 (ceiling engages), NORMAL 39/40 (seed 25 still stands), HARD 38/40. pongcheck 66/66, mutants 13+5 all die, new pongdrive 18/18 in real Chrome with pixel-vs-logic paddle checks.

The never-dry kick named DEFENDER, but that index was a stage-narrative bullet owned by QA #3497 — walked the scoreboard manually and found PONG with 5 genuinely unowned gaps. The QA polish pass (#3506) quotes the README's by-design gaps verbatim so the ownership matcher can't ghost them again.

look.text: Pick your table: EASY · NORMAL · HARD · 2P on the PONG attract screen
